newsitem.title: UK: BBC World Service increases audience in 1996.
newsitem.headline: BBC World Service increases audience in 1996.

text.p: Up to 143 million people in 140 countries listen to the British Broadcasting Corporation's World Service every week, the BBC said on Monday.
The new figures for the government-funded radio service, which broadcasts in 45 languages, mark an increase of three million in the past year.
They include estimates for the 10 largest cities in China but exclude audience numbers for Burma, Cuba and Iran where reliable research is not available.

"The new audience estimate shows the importance of our plans to acquire new FM and medium wave outlets around the world to reach new listeners and keep our existing fans," Caroline Thomas, deputy managing director of BBC World Service, said.
"The five million pounds ($8 million) reinstated by the government to our budget last November has allowed us to continue with this vital programme," she said in a statement.
The latest figures show an increase in audience size in Poland and French-speaking countries in Africa, but a drop in Nigeria and Kenya.
Thirty-five million people listen to the BBC World Service in English each week, including 1.3 million in Britain.
